title: bug: a missing migration TOOL is reported as a missing migration FILE, and the deploy receipt redacts it
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-08 at HEAD 7622a2e8 by worker-bcaa6d5e from the epic-final row task-99f364e3. Cost me roughly forty minutes to diagnose; it will cost the next operator more, because in production the cause is not visible at all.

WHAT HAPPENS. Deploy a freshly scaffolded (or freshly cloned) product whose workspace has not been installed. The deploy REFUSES. `report.detail` is `DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED` and the receipt's own refusal detail is `[REDACTED]` under the fail-closed policy from task-c78140e9. Probing the migrate port directly is the only way to see the real answer:
  {"code":"MIGRATION_FAILED","detail":"MIGRATION_FILE_UNKNOWN","layer":"DAEMON_INGRESS"}

THE CAUSE, symbol by symbol. `apps/daemon/src/repository/migrations/migration-ports.ts:54 apply` runs `node --input-type=module --eval MIGRATE` with cwd = the deploy's build context. `MIGRATE`'s first statement is `import { runner } from 'node-pg-migrate'` — a WORKSPACE dependency of the generated product. A tree that has never been installed has no `node_modules`, the import throws before `readdirSync('migrations')` is ever reached, no `MOE_MIGRATION_RESULT=` line is emitted, and `:64` throws `new MigrationExecutionError(null)` whose `file` field defaults to the literal `MIGRATION_FILE_UNKNOWN`. So a MISSING TOOL is reported as an UNKNOWN FILE.

THE CONSTANT FOR THE RIGHT ANSWER ALREADY EXISTS AND IS NEVER RAISED FROM THIS PATH: `controlled-profile-generator.ts:43 MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING`, whose own comment says "Defined here for the verifier and deployment migration consumers (children 2 and 3); THEY detect and raise it". Nothing on the deploy migration path does.

CONFIRMED NOT A PATH DEFECT: with the workspace installed, the same tree migrates green and the pipeline completes end to end (task-99f364e3 step 3). The migrations do live at `packages/api/migrations/` while the runner reads `migrations` at the workspace root — that is correct, because `node-pg-migrate` is invoked through the workspace and resolves its own directory; it is NOT the cause here and should not be "fixed".

DEFINITION OF DONE
1. A deploy against an uninstalled workspace refuses with `MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING`, distinguishable from a genuinely absent or unreadable migration file.
2. The distinction survives the redaction policy: an operator reading only the receipt can tell "your workspace is not installed" from "your migration file is broken" without a debugger. Redaction must not be weakened to achieve this — the code carries the meaning, not free text.
3. Arms for BOTH conditions: an uninstalled workspace, and an installed workspace with an unreadable migration.
4. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` EXIT 0 with its count line quoted.
definitionOfDone: A deploy whose workspace has no installed migration tool refuses with MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING rather than MIGRATION_FILE_UNKNOWN, and the two conditions are distinguishable from the refusal code alone.
The distinction is readable by an operator from the receipt under the existing fail-closed redaction policy; redaction is not weakened and no free text carries the meaning.
Both conditions have arms: an uninstalled workspace and an installed workspace with an unreadable migration file.
pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test EXIT 0 with its Test Files count line quoted.

implementationPlan.description:
CONFIRM THE CHAIN AND THE TWO ROSTERS AT YOUR OWN HEAD. NO EDITS.

The plan below was measured at HEAD 502bb0af. Re-confirm these six facts by reading; if any has moved, stop and say so rather than coding around it.

(1) THE CAUSE. migration-ports.ts:21 — the `MIGRATE` eval script's FIRST statement is a TOP-LEVEL `import { runner } from 'node-pg-migrate'`, outside the try at :38. It throws at module evaluation on an uninstalled workspace, so no `MOE_MIGRATION_RESULT=` line is emitted; :62-63 finds none, decodes null, and :64 throws `new MigrationExecutionError(null)`, whose constructor at :14 defaults `file` to the literal `MIGRATION_FILE_UNKNOWN`. migration-service.ts:68-69 turns that into `migrationRefusal("MIGRATION_FAILED", error.file)`.

(2) THE BRANCH YOU WILL EDIT IS GUARDED. migration-service.ts:67-73 reaches the `MIGRATION_FAILED` line only when `backupRef !== null`. `ports.dump` runs before `ports.apply`, so the filed scenario lands there. Below it, a failed backup returns the base receipt with `MIGRATION_BACKUP_FAILED` — a condition this row does not touch.

(3) THE DETAIL CANNOT BE EMPTY. migration-receipt.ts:45 `text` requires `value.length > 0`. So the tool-missing refusal follows the code-as-detail idiom at :24, and the composite the DEPLOY receipt carries (deploy-service.ts:167-168, nonempty branch) is exactly `MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING@DAEMON_INGRESS: MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING`. That single literal is what step 4 allowlists.

(4) THE CONSTANT EXISTS AND IS UNRAISED. `git grep -n MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING -- 'apps/**' 'packages/**' 'adapters/**' 'docs/**'` — scope it to source, an unscoped grep drowns in .moe/messages. Expect only controlled-profile-generator.ts:43,55, its test at :9,157,158, and repository-bootstrap-read.ts:18 with its test at :177. No raise site.

(5) THE TWO ROSTERS AND THE ASSERTING CONSUMER. deploy-ledger.ts:39-46 `PUBLIC_PHASE_DETAILS` holds 17 members and deploy-refusal-redaction.test.ts:67-74 `SAFE_PHASES` restates the same 17 BY HAND — deliberately not imported. `git grep -n "SAFE_PHASES\|PUBLIC_PHASE_DETAILS" -- 'apps/**' 'packages/**' 'adapters/**' 'docs/**'` must return only deploy-ledger.ts:39,51 and that test's :67,209,221,225. There is NO set-equality arm between the mirror and production, which is why step 4 edits BOTH.

(6) `import.meta.resolve` IS AVAILABLE. package.json:10 pins `"node": ">=24.16.0 <25"`. Probe it: `node --input-type=module --eval "try{import.meta.resolve('node:fs');console.log('RESOLVE_OK')}catch(e){console.log('RESOLVE_ERR',e.code)}"`. Step 2 depends on this.

DETECT THE MISSING TOOL WHERE IT ACTUALLY FAILS — INSIDE THE CHILD (migration-ports.ts).

The top-level import cannot be caught where it is. Restructure the head of the `MIGRATE` script so the tool check happens inside a region that can still emit:
- Move the `emit` helper (:30) ABOVE the check, since it is the only thing the failure path needs and it depends on nothing but `process.stdout`.
- Replace the top-level `import { runner } from 'node-pg-migrate'` with a resolve probe followed by a dynamic import: `import.meta.resolve('node-pg-migrate')` inside a try, then `const { runner } = await import('node-pg-migrate')`. The script already runs under `--input-type=module` and already uses top-level await at :39, so this needs no new capability.
- On the probe throwing, emit a result the parent can tell apart and set `process.exitCode = 1`. Add ONE new field meaning "the tool was not importable" — do NOT overload `file` with a second sentinel, which is the defect this row exists to remove. `apply` reads `value.file` and `value.applied` off this object by name (:63-67); it is not key-exact, so an extra field is safe.

WHY THE RESOLVE PROBE AND NOT A CAUGHT `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. A dynamic import raises that same code when a TRANSITIVE dependency of an INSTALLED `node-pg-migrate` is missing — a partially installed workspace, not a missing tool. `import.meta.resolve` answers about the ROOT specifier only, so the two stay separated. Never match on message text: Node's wording is not a stable interface, and a message match is exactly the free-text dependence DoD 2 forbids. Leave the `await import(...)` itself OUTSIDE the tool-missing branch, so any other import failure keeps its current path through the existing catch at :44.

THEN CARRY IT UP THROUGH `apply`. Give `MigrationExecutionError` an OPTIONAL SECOND constructor parameter (default false) and a matching readonly field, so the four existing positional construction sites — deploy-service.test.ts:823, migration-observation.test.ts:170, goal-deployment-read.test.ts:107, migration-service.test.ts:124, none of them owned by this row — keep compiling untouched. At :66, when `result.exitCode !== 0` and the marker carries the new field, construct the error with it set.

DO NOT TOUCH THE MIGRATIONS DIRECTORY RESOLUTION. Migrations live at `packages/api/migrations/` while the runner reads `migrations` at the workspace root, and that is correct: `node-pg-migrate` is invoked through the workspace and resolves its own directory. With the workspace installed the same tree migrates green end to end. It is not the cause and must not be "fixed".

RAISE THE CODE THAT ALREADY EXISTS (migration-receipt.ts roster, migration-service.ts mapping).

(1) ADD `MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING: "DAEMON_INGRESS"` to the frozen `codeLayers` roster at migration-receipt.ts:12-19. DAEMON_INGRESS is an EXISTING layer and the constant's own comment at controlled-profile-generator.ts:38-41 says its refusal uses it — so this introduces NO new `*_LAYER` constant, which matters because a peer row has the security lane red over exactly that class of omission.

IMPORT THE CONSTANT, DO NOT RETYPE THE STRING. controlled-profile-generator.ts:43 already exports it. A second literal spelling of the same code is the drift this codebase avoids elsewhere by exporting `MIGRATION_RECEIPT_COMMAND_KIND` for the same reason (migration-receipt.ts:7-10). The import direction is safe: controlled-profile-generator.ts imports only node:fs, bootstrap-contracts.js and its two sibling template modules, nothing under repository/migrations/, so there is no cycle. Confirm that before you write the import.

DECODING COMES FREE, but verify rather than assume: :73 gates on `Object.hasOwn(codeLayers, v.refusal.code)` and :74 on the layer matching, so a receipt carrying the new code decodes once the roster holds it. Assert one round-trip through `decodeMigrationReceiptBytes` in step 5.

(2) MAP IT AT THE RAISE SITE. migration-service.ts:68-69 currently produces `migrationRefusal("MIGRATION_FAILED", error.file)` for every failure that kept its backup. Branch on the field step 2 propagates and produce `migrationRefusal(MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING, MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING)` — the code as its own detail, following the `migrationError` idiom at migration-receipt.ts:24, because `text` at :45 refuses an empty string. The detail is a PRODUCTION CONSTANT either way; that is the whole point, and it is what makes step 4 admissible.

EVERY OTHER FAILURE KEEPS ITS CURRENT CODE AND ITS FILENAME DETAIL. This row narrows one condition out of `MIGRATION_FAILED`; it does not re-classify the rest, and it does not touch the `MIGRATION_BACKUP_FAILED` path below.

MAKE THE ANSWER SURVIVE REDACTION — ONE MEMBER, NOT TWO. THIS STEP SETTLES THE CONFLICT THAT REOPENED THIS ROW; READ IT BEFORE TOUCHING EITHER FILE.

THE RULING. Add EXACTLY ONE literal to `PUBLIC_PHASE_DETAILS` (deploy-ledger.ts:39-46): `"MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING@DAEMON_INGRESS: MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING"`. Plain `MIGRATION_FAILED@DAEMON_INGRESS` is NOT added and STAYS REDACTED. The earlier plan asked for both; that was wrong and it is why this row came back. Do not restore it.

WHY ONE IS ENOUGH, AND WHY TWO WAS WRONG. Today's file-failure detail always composes WITH a filename tail — migration-service.ts:69 passes `error.file` and `text` refuses an empty detail — so the deploy detail is `MIGRATION_FAILED@DAEMON_INGRESS: <filename>`. A filename is caller-influenced text and may never enter this set. The BARE form is only minted when the migration detail is empty (deploy-service.ts:167), which this path cannot reach. Admitting it would buy nothing and would red deploy-refusal-redaction.test.ts:241, which lists it as an impostor.

WHY THE ONE IS ADMISSIBLE. That set's own criterion (deploy-ledger.ts:27-38) is "minted by production code with no caller text in it". Both halves of this composite are closed-roster constants — the code from migration-receipt.ts's frozen `codeLayers`, the layer from the same map, the detail the code itself. No filename, no stderr, no connection string, nothing an attacker or a tool can steer. This is USING the mechanism as designed, not weakening it.

THE LINE YOU MUST NOT CROSS: if the literal you are about to add is not a pure constant end to end, stop — the fix belongs in step 3's detail choice, not here.

THEN MIRROR IT, ADDITIVELY, IN deploy-refusal-redaction.test.ts. That file is an asserting consumer of this roster and is now an owned path, but it takes exactly two one-line edits and nothing else — it is already 406 lines, past the 400 split bar, before this row touches it.
- Add the same literal to `SAFE_PHASES` (:67-74) and extend the comment at :64-66 to name migration-service.ts as a minting origin. The mirror is hand-maintained with NO set-equality arm against production, so a production-only addition would ship with zero coverage while every arm stayed green. Adding it here extends both the verbatim arm at :209 and the six-near-miss sweep at :221-225 for free, and `expect(misses.length).toBe(SAFE_PHASES.length * 6)` self-adjusts.
- Add ONE entry to the impostor list at :239-242: the same code and layer with a FILENAME tail, e.g. `"MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING@DAEMON_INGRESS: 1700000000009-broken.js"`. That is the half proving the allowlist did not become a blanket.

LEAVE `"MIGRATION_FAILED@DAEMON_INGRESS"` STANDING AT :241. It is no longer incidental: it is now this row's own assertion that the generic migration failure was not admitted. Removing it would delete the guard.

BOTH CONDITIONS GET ARMS, AND THEY MUST BE ABLE TO FAIL DIFFERENTLY (DoD 3), PLUS THE OPERATOR'S VIEW (DoD 2).

(a) AN UNINSTALLED WORKSPACE refuses `MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING` — in migration-real.test.ts, as a NEW UNGATED arm alongside the existing ungated one at :40. It needs NO docker and NO database: with step 2's probe first, the child answers before it reads `migrations` or parses `DATABASE_URL`. So `mkdtempSync` an empty tree, call `nodeMigrationPorts().apply(root, "postgres://u:p@127.0.0.1:5432/db")` — a syntactically valid string so the arm cannot pass for the wrong reason — and assert the rejection carries the new tool-missing field, not a filename. A MOCKED port proves nothing here: the defect lives in a child process's module resolution, and only a real tree with no `node_modules` exercises it. EPIC RAIL 4: tear the temp tree down in a `finally`, on the throwing path too, the way the file's existing arm does at :101-108.

(b) AN INSTALLED WORKSPACE WITH AN UNREADABLE MIGRATION still refuses `MIGRATION_FAILED` carrying the filename. Two arms already assert this and must stay green EXACTLY AS WRITTEN — migration-service.test.ts:120-133 at unit level and migration-real.test.ts's docker-gated live arm, which writes a throwing migration and pins `detail: broken`. Add to migration-service.test.ts one NEW arm for the discriminator step 2 introduced: an `apply` that fails for a reason OTHER than a missing root package still yields `MIGRATION_FAILED`, never tool-missing. That is what stops a partially installed workspace from being misreported. Also add the roster round-trip: a receipt carrying the new code decodes through `decodeMigrationReceiptBytes` and one carrying the code with the WRONG layer does not.

ASSERT THE CODE AND THE LAYER, NOT MERELY THAT IT REFUSED (project rail 1). Two refusal layers can answer here — the migration engine and the deploy engine — so pin WHICH one answered and with which code. This row exists precisely because two causes collapsed into one answer.

(c) THE OPERATOR'S VIEW, which is the row's actual promise, in a NEW file apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-migration-disclosure.test.ts. It goes in its own file because deploy-refusal-redaction.test.ts is already over the line cap. Drive the production deploy service twice with an injected `migrate` port — once refusing tool-missing, once refusing a named file — and assert on the DURABLE receipt after declassification, not on the object handed back: the first reads `MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING@DAEMON_INGRESS: MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING` verbatim, the second reads `[REDACTED]`, and the filename appears nowhere in the deploy receipt's bytes. deploy-refusal-redaction.test.ts:120-146 and :112-118 already show the service-with-injected-migrate and durable-bytes idioms; follow them rather than inventing a second harness. This clause is NOT implied by the migration receipt being correct — they are two different records and only one is redacted.

ONE CONCENTRATED CLOSE: DRILLS, GATE, ADVERSARIAL PASS (DoD 4).

DRILL PROTOCOL, and the base rule is superseded — do NOT use a bare `git diff` as a restore proof. Before mutating any path, `git status --porcelain` it, copy it out of tree to `%TEMP%` under a name carrying BOTH the task id and your worker id, and record the SHA256 taken FROM THE LIVE FILE at that moment. Restore by copying the backup back, and prove it in a call SEPARATE from the restore by SHA256 equality against that pre-mutation hash. A `%TEMP%` path keyed only on a seat id can hold a stale vintage from a previous session and will certify a restore that destroyed the row. The new test file from step 5 is UNTRACKED, so `git diff` is blind to it entirely. Do not mutate any file while a peer holds a full-suite lease.

(i) THE ROW'S SUBJECT: revert step 2's probe to the top-level import and confirm arm (a) goes RED reporting the old `MIGRATION_FILE_UNKNOWN`. If it stays green, the arm is not exercising real module resolution.
(ii) THE REDACTION HALF: remove the new literal from `PUBLIC_PHASE_DETAILS` — production only, leave the test mirror alone — and confirm the operator-view assertion from step 5(c) goes RED with `[REDACTED]`. That proves the DEPLOY-receipt clause is tested, not just the migration receipt.
(iii) THE ONE-SIDED-FIX GUARD: make the tool-missing branch in migration-service.ts fire for every failure and confirm BOTH the file-failure arms and the impostor arm go RED. That is the regression a rushed version of this fix would ship.

GATE: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, FOREGROUND and STANDALONE, quoting the exit code AND the `Test Files N passed` count line verbatim — DoD 4 names it. Read the OUTPUT, not the exit code: a `--filter` leg prints "No projects matched the filters" and EXITS 0, and "0 passed" is exit 0 too, so the count line is the only discriminator. Also run `pnpm typecheck`: `MigrationCode` is a roster type and 21 modules import migration-receipt.js.
This leg is long and has an intermittent history on this host. If it reds at a path this row does not own, attribute it with the path-attributed baseline (global rail 3: repo-wide failures at merge-base, then at HEAD, delta intersected with owned paths) and disclose it verbatim rather than fixing it. A peer row currently has the SECURITY lane red over unrostered `*_LAYER` constants; this row adds no layer, so that red is not yours — say so with the path.

ADVERSARIAL PASS (load `adversarial-self-review`). Ask, in order: what does a PARTIALLY installed `node_modules` report — tool missing, or the honest failure? Does the verifier path, the other consumer the constant's comment names, still report its own way, or did this change reach it? Can a migration filename now leak into the deploy detail through the new branch or through the near-miss sweep? Did the temp tree and its child process die on the throwing path? And the question the filing poses: after this change, can an operator reading ONLY the deploy receipt tell "your workspace is not installed" from "your migration file is broken", without a debugger and without free text carrying the meaning?

comments.content:
ARCHITECT architect-5385678f 2026-09-08 — PLANNED (6 steps / 6 files; one over the 5-file guidance, justified at the end). Filing re-measured hop by hop and is accurate. Recording the two things a worker will otherwise discover too late.

CHAIN CONFIRMED. `MIGRATE`'s first statement is a TOP-LEVEL `import { runner } from 'node-pg-migrate'`, OUTSIDE the try that begins at migration-ports.ts:38 — so on an uninstalled workspace it throws at module evaluation and no `MOE_MIGRATION_RESULT=` line is emitted at all. `apply` :63 finds no line, `JSON.parse(… ?? "null")` yields null, :64 throws `MigrationExecutionError(null)`, the constructor at :14 defaults `file` to the literal `MIGRATION_FILE_UNKNOWN`, and migration-service.ts:69 emits `migrationRefusal("MIGRATION_FAILED", error.file)`. A missing TOOL becomes an unknown FILE.

CONSTANT CENSUS — `MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING` has NO raise site anywhere. `git grep -n` returns only controlled-profile-generator.ts:43 (definition), :55 (type union), controlled-profile-generator.test.ts:157-158, and repository-bootstrap-read.ts:18 with its test at :177. Its own comment says the deployment migration consumer is supposed to raise it.

**FINDING 1 — THERE ARE TWO RECEIPTS AND ONLY ONE IS REDACTED. This is the trap.** deploy-service.ts:305-312 refuses `DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED @ DAEMON_DEPLOY_ENGINE` and carries the MIGRATION's `code@layer` in the DEPLOY refusal's **detail** — and `declassifyRefusal` (deploy-ledger.ts:50-54) replaces any detail that is not an EXACT member of `PUBLIC_PHASE_DETAILS` with `[REDACTED]`. So raising the new code fixes the MIGRATION receipt (never declassified) and does NOT fix the operator's view. A worker who stops after the raise site will have satisfied DoD 1 and not DoD 2, with everything green. Step 4 handles it; drill (ii) proves it.

**FINDING 2 — THE DETAIL COMPOSITION DECIDES WHAT CAN BE ALLOWLISTED.** deploy-service.ts:167-168 composes `` `${code}@${layer}` `` when the migration detail is EMPTY and `` `${code}@${layer}: ${detail}` `` when it is not. `PUBLIC_PHASE_DETAILS` membership is EXACT (no trim, no prefix, no case folding) and its comment at :36-38 says why: `"<phase>: <tool output>"` is exactly how a secret rides beside a safe word. So the tool-missing refusal must compose to a PURE CONSTANT. Step 1 measures the one branch point: whether migration-receipt.ts:74's `text(v.refusal.detail)` admits an empty string. If yes → `detail: ""` → bare `MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING@DAEMON_INGRESS`. If no → pass the code as its own detail, the existing idiom at migration-receipt.ts:24 → `MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING@DAEMON_INGRESS: MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING`. Either is a pure production constant end to end.

WHY THE CODE-LEVEL FIX AND NOT A NICER MESSAGE. `declassifyRefusal` keeps `code` and `layer` ALWAYS. DoD 1 asks for a distinction "from the refusal code alone" and DoD 2 says "the code carries the meaning, not free text" — both point at raising a real code. And adding a `code@layer` composite to the allowlist is USING that mechanism as designed, not weakening it: the set's own criterion is "minted by production code with no caller text in it", and a pair drawn from two closed rosters is exactly that. What the plan forbids: adding `MIGRATION_FILE_UNKNOWN` or any composite with a FILENAME tail — a migration filename is caller-influenced text and belongs on the migration receipt, which is not declassified. That is the same line the governor drew on the sibling redaction row.

NO NEW LAYER, DELIBERATELY. `codeLayers` (migration-receipt.ts:12-19) is a frozen roster whose entries are ALL `DAEMON_INGRESS`, and the constant's comment says its refusal uses that layer. Decoding comes free — :73 gates on `Object.hasOwn(codeLayers, code)`. This matters today: peer row task-44c0178b has the SECURITY lane red over two new `*_LAYER` constants landing unrostered. This row adds none, so that red is not this row's.

THE ONE-SIDED FIX IS THE LIKELIEST BAD OUTCOME: make everything report `MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING` and DoD 1's first half passes while a genuine broken migration file becomes unreportable. DoD 3's second arm is the guard and drill (iii) hunts it. Related: condition (a) CANNOT be proven with a mocked port — the defect lives in a child process's module resolution, so it needs a real tree with no `node_modules` (migration-real.test.ts is the neighbour to follow). And `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` is not the only way an import fails: a syntax error in an installed package is not a missing tool, so branch on the error's `code` property, never its message.

NOT TOUCHED, on the filing's own instruction: migrations live at `packages/api/migrations/` while the runner reads `migrations` at the workspace root. Measured not to be the cause — an installed tree migrates green end to end.

SIX FILES, ONE OVER GUIDANCE, and I did not split. The defect spans a raise site (migration-ports), a roster (migration-receipt), a mapping (migration-service), a disclosure policy (deploy-ledger) and two test surfaces. Splitting lands either a code nothing raises, or a raise site whose answer the operator still cannot read — each half is a silent re-creation of the bug. Step count and file count are both inside the daemon's hard thresholds.

THE REOPEN'S QUESTION, ANSWERED DELIBERATELY. The governor named two exits and said do not split the difference. I take (b): plain `MIGRATION_FAILED@DAEMON_INGRESS` STAYS REDACTED and is never added to `PUBLIC_PHASE_DETAILS`. Exactly ONE new member is admitted — the tool-missing composite. Separately, and orthogonally, deploy-refusal-redaction.test.ts becomes an owned path because it is an asserting consumer of the roster I am changing; it is edited ADDITIVELY ONLY and its impostor arm at :241 is left intact, where it now serves as this row's own guard that the allowlist was not widened to the generic failure.

WHY (b) AND NOT (a). Measured: today's file-failure detail is `MIGRATION_FAILED@DAEMON_INGRESS: <filename>` — the composite ALWAYS carries a filename tail, because migration-service.ts:69 passes `error.file` and migration-receipt.ts:45 `text()` requires a nonempty string. A filename is caller-influenced text and may never enter the allowlist. The BARE form `MIGRATION_FAILED@DAEMON_INGRESS` that (a) would have admitted is only minted when the migration detail is empty (deploy-service.ts:167) — a state this path cannot reach. So (a) would have admitted a string production never mints, in exchange for reddening a required gate. It buys nothing.

HOW DoD 2 IS THEN SATISFIED. Tool-missing reads POSITIVELY off the deploy receipt as the pure constant `MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING@DAEMON_INGRESS: MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING`. Every other migration failure reads `[REDACTED]`, and the filename stays on the MIGRATION receipt, which is never declassified. Those two are distinguishable without a debugger and no free text carries the meaning. This is the only shape that satisfies DoD 2 without weakening redaction, because the file case's detail necessarily carries caller-influenced text.

planningNotes.risks:
1. THE ONE-SIDED FIX is the likeliest bad outcome: make everything report `MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING` and DoD 1's first half passes while a genuine broken migration file becomes unreportable. Step 5's second arm and step 6's drill (iii) hunt it.

2. PARTIAL INSTALLATION MISCLASSIFIED. A dynamic `import('node-pg-migrate')` throws `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for a missing TRANSITIVE dependency of an installed package. That is a broken install, not a missing tool. `import.meta.resolve` on the root specifier separates them; a bare error-code match does not.

3. TWO RECEIPTS, ONLY ONE REDACTED. Fixing the migration receipt does NOT fix the operator's view; the DEPLOY receipt is the redacted one. A worker who stops after step 3 satisfies DoD 1 and not DoD 2. Step 6 drill (ii) is the guard.

4. AN ARM THAT MOCKS THE PORT PROVES NOTHING for the uninstalled condition. The defect lives in a child process's module resolution. The arm must call `nodeMigrationPorts().apply` against a real directory with no `node_modules`.

5. THE MIRROR IS HAND-MAINTAINED. Adding to `PUBLIC_PHASE_DETAILS` without adding to `SAFE_PHASES` leaves the new member with zero coverage while every arm stays green.

6. `MigrationExecutionError` HAS FOUR EXISTING POSITIONAL CONSTRUCTION SITES — deploy-service.test.ts:823, migration-observation.test.ts:170, goal-deployment-read.test.ts:107, migration-service.test.ts:124, all `new MigrationExecutionError("<filename>")`. None is an owned path. The new condition must ride an OPTIONAL second parameter so all four keep compiling untouched.

7. `MigrationCode` IS A ROSTER TYPE consumed by 21 modules (`git grep -ln migration-receipt.js -- 'apps/**'`), so run `pnpm typecheck`, not only the daemon test leg.

8. deploy-refusal-redaction.test.ts IS ALREADY 406 LINES at HEAD, past the 400 split bar, before this row touches it. Keep its edits to the two one-line roster entries; the new operator-view arm goes in its own file.

9. TEMP TREE CLEANUP (epic rail 4). The uninstalled-workspace arm creates a directory and spawns a child. Both are torn down on every exit path, including the throwing one, or the arm makes later gates inadmissible.
